“你没有做错任何事。”（你在说谎。）
“你已将这座村庄判了死刑。”

开场 1：一支缀满花朵、色彩艳俗而喧闹的游行队伍穿过村庄，朝十字路口行进。今晚这里想必有好几百人，甚至更多。你与马奎兹博士并肩走向那座阴森的雕像，雕像上反射的灯光旋转不休。蕾切尔嬷嬷站在人群中央，双臂像树枝一样朝那棵镜面之树伸出。

查看你的战役日志。
如果马奎兹博士有了计划，前往 开场 2。
否则，跳到 开场 5。

开场 2：教授牵着丽贝卡的手大步走上前。蕾切尔嬷嬷转过身来，所有庆祝活动都停了下来。“大家听我说！昨晚，蕾切尔嬷嬷把一屋子病人判了死刑。我当时在场。他们神智并不清醒。”马奎兹博士向赴宴者们恳求道。“但这还不是全部。这座岛底下有东西活着。它正在吸干周围一切的生命，可能毁掉整个村庄。我们必须立刻离开这座岛！”蕾切尔嬷嬷受伤般地看着你。“你在指控我什么？我把女儿献作祭品，而她又被还给了我。”

查看你的战役日志。调查员们必须做出决定（选择一项）：
“你没有做错任何事。”前往 开场 3。（只有当蕾切尔嬷嬷的关系等级达到 3 或更高时，你才能选择此项。）
“你没有做错任何事。”（你在说谎。）跳到 开场 4。（只有当蕾切尔嬷嬷的关系等级达到 3 或更高时，你才能选择此项。）
“你已将这座村庄判了死刑。”跳到 开场 5。

开场 3：你走上前，俯身在蕾切尔嬷嬷脚边，马奎兹博士不由得倒吸一口气。女家长温和地看着你。“非常欢迎你加入我们的餐桌。你可以坐在我的右手边，好亲眼看看今天有什么奇迹在等着我们。”她以铁箍般的力道紧紧握住你的手，领你走向盛宴。你顺从地跟在她身后。

在本战役余下的时间里，将 1 枚 [cultist] 标记加入混乱袋。

在每位调查员的牌库中搜寻罗莎·马奎兹博士剧情支援，并将其移出游戏。

在你的战役日志中记录调查员们信了。

开场 4：你朝马奎兹博士使了个眼色，然后走上前，向蕾切尔嬷嬷鞠躬。女家长温和地看着你。“非常欢迎你加入我们的餐桌。你可以坐在我的右手边，好亲眼看看今天有什么奇迹在等着我们。”她以铁箍般的力道紧紧握住你的手，领你走向盛宴。你警惕地跟在她身后。

在本战役余下的时间里，将 1 枚 [cultist] 标记和 1 枚 [elder_thing] 标记加入混乱袋。

在你的战役日志中记录调查员们对蕾切尔嬷嬷撒了谎。

开场 5：教授大步走上前，在狂欢的喧嚣中高声喊道。“这里的食物有毒！你们全都身处险境：不管这东西是什么，它正在改变周围的一切。看见了吗？”马奎兹博士一张接一张地扯下赴宴者的面具，露出他们狂乱而咧嘴大笑的脸。周围的人群静了下来。接着响起一阵掌声，还有笑声。蕾切尔嬷嬷举起双臂，让人群安静。“把这些诽谤者赶出去！但别让他们妨碍我们的庆典。天国在召唤我们！让我们开宴！”

你被推离喧嚣时，最后看到的是女家长那得意的笑容。

在本战役余下的时间里，将 1 枚 [tablet] 标记和 1 枚 [elder_thing] 标记加入混乱袋。

在你的战役日志中记录调查员们打断了盛宴。

setup.text: 收集下列遭遇组的所有卡牌：最终之日、盛宴之日、居民与山谷。
将 第三日 时间标记卡放入游戏。你准备好了吗？
使用《围坐桌边》组建幕与议程牌库。它同时是当前的幕与当前的议程。将《待宰羔羊》特殊议程放置一旁。将其他所有幕与议程移出游戏。
按照第 6 页的地图，将除十字路口与老磨坊以外的每个地点以其 (第三日) 面放入游戏。
使用盛宴之日遭遇组中的十字路口与老磨坊地点，(晚上) 面朝上。将其他十字路口与老磨坊地点移出游戏。
将 1 张狂乱的赴宴者敌人卡放入集会厅。如果游戏中有 3 或 4 名调查员，将另一张狂乱的赴宴者放入毒堇教堂。
收集居民遭遇组，并查看战役日志。
如果“已勘察区域”下的北岬矿井尚未勾选，划去莉亚·阿特伍德的名字。然后将名字已被划去的每位居民移出游戏。
将蕾切尔嬷嬷以资产面朝上放入十字路口。将莉亚·阿特伍德放入毒堇教堂、席米恩·阿特伍德放入山谷学校、基甸·米兹拉克放入集会厅、朱迪斯·帕克放入老磨坊、希奥·彼得斯放入泰德杂货店，均以资产面朝上（若某位居民的关系等级处于或低于所列阈值，则将其翻至敌人面）。如果伯蒂灵光一闪，将伯蒂·马斯格雷夫以敌人面朝上放入十字路口。如果调查员们打断了盛宴，将马奎兹博士放入游戏，由一名调查员控制。
将其他每位居民放置一旁，置于游戏外。
如果调查员们打断了盛宴，每位调查员从旅舍开始游戏。否则，每位调查员从十字路口开始游戏。
在议程上放置毁灭标记，数量等于调查员数量。

children.text:
《铁杉谷盛宴》战役引入了一个全新的玩法概念：铁杉谷法典。在这场战役中，有些卡牌效果会指示玩家阅读特定的法典条目。游玩时请将战役指南放在手边，方便随时查阅。

《铁杉谷盛宴》中的某些地点、角色或敌人拥有法典条目，标记为（[codex] X）。要阅读某个角色或地点的法典条目，你必须先支付该能力上的所有费用，然后翻到本战役指南中当前关卡或序曲的法典部分，结算全部文本。

• 除非另有说明，每个法典条目在每场关卡或序曲中不能结算超过一次。

• 结算法典条目时，由触发该条目的玩家结算全部效果（进行检定、造成伤害、支付资源等）。如果无法确定是谁触发了该法典条目，则由队长结算该条目。

• 如果法典条目指示玩家将某位放在一边的具名居民加入游戏，除非另有说明，该角色以剧情支援面朝上加入游戏。

• 战役日志中名字已被划去的居民不能在序曲或关卡中进入游戏。如果某位居民的名字已被划去，该居民笔记中的全部条目也同样失效。

• 在为某个特定角色结算法典条目时，你只能阅读自己满足条件的单个小节。如果你不满足法典条目第一个小节的条件，就跳到下一个小节。除非另有说明，只参考该角色在你战役日志中的笔记与关系等级。（例如：“在瑞玟·霍桑的笔记中记录瑞玟是个万人迷”是指让玩家修改瑞玟战役日志条目中的“笔记”部分。）

• 结算完法典条目并在战役日志中做好变更后，恢复游戏。

《铁杉谷盛宴》战役只给玩家游戏内的三天时间来把整个故事走完。本战役还包含可游玩的序曲，调查员可以在其中与铁杉谷的居民互动、探寻铁杉岛的秘密，并为下一场关卡做准备。序曲是非对抗性的段落，会设置地点、剧本参考卡、幕与议程。每段序曲结束时都会给出若干选项，决定接下来游玩哪场关卡。视日期与时段而定，有些关卡会提供新的剧情选项或挑战。在一次战役的通关过程中，玩家没有时间游玩每一场关卡，也无法与每一位居民都交上朋友。

• 玩家在游玩序曲与幕间时可以赚取经验。把这些经验记录在“未花费经验”下，但在战役指南指示之前不要花费。

• 要掌握当前的日期／时段，你可以查看并更新战役日志中的“日期／时段”部分。

有时，剧情文本会指示调查员提高他们与某位特定居民的关系等级。若接到此类指示，请查看战役日志，找到该指定居民的条目。

• 提到某位居民的关系等级时，其条目中已勾选的格数就是该居民的关系等级。

• 要提高某位居民的关系等级，勾选该居民条目中最左侧未勾选的格子。

• 要降低某位居民的关系等级，擦掉该居民条目中最右侧已勾选的格子。

• 除非另有说明，每次只能提高或降低某位居民 1 格关系等级。

• 若接到将某位居民的关系等级设为 0 的指示，擦掉该居民条目中所有已勾选的格子。

• 战役日志中名字已被划去的居民不能在序曲或关卡中进入游戏。

本战役中的多数关卡按固定的网格样式摆放地点。在这些关卡中，每个地点除了连接图标之外，还与和它相邻的每个地点相连。

• 相邻的地点共享一条边（左边、右边、上方或下方）。只共享一个角的地点不算相邻。

• 接到将地点加入游戏的指示时，把它放在你所在地点上方、下方、左侧或右侧的相邻空位。

• 你不能把地点放到已有地点所在的位置上。选择新地点的位置时，若有可能，你必须选一个没有被地点占据的位置。若无法做到，则不将任何新地点加入游戏。

• 注意，在使用了“山谷”遭遇组的序曲与关卡中，地点只通过其图标相连。
本战役中的某些敌人拥有警戒关键词。每当调查员在尝试躲避拥有警戒关键词的敌人时技能检定失败，在结算完该次技能检定的所有结果之后，该敌人会对躲避它的调查员执行一次攻击。敌人在执行警戒攻击后不会横置。无论该敌人是否与躲避它的调查员交战，这次攻击都会发生。

在本战役中设置游戏时，玩家可能会被指示将时间标记卡加入游戏。为此，请从第一日、第二日或最终日遭遇组中找到与当前日期对应的时间标记卡，并将它放在议程牌库旁。这张卡代表当前的日期与时段。

有些卡牌会根据关卡发生在白日还是黑夜而产生不同效果。以（白日 [day]）或（黑夜 [night]）关键词开头的文本，只有所游玩的关卡或序曲分别处于白日或黑夜时才生效。前面没有这些关键词的任何其他能力，不论时段如何都生效。

设置指示可能会根据当前的日期与时段给出特定指示。（例如：“如果当前是第二日，将瑞玟·霍桑在蔓越莓沼泽加入游戏”这条指示只在把该关卡作为第二日关卡游玩时生效，在第二夜关卡中不生效。）

本战役中的某些敌人拥有逃逸关键词。逃逸敌人代表为了自保或达成自己的目标而想避开调查员的敌人。

如果处于重整状态且拥有逃逸关键词的敌人攻击或被攻击，在该次攻击结算之后，该敌人立即与所有调查员解除交战，移动到一个相连地点（若有可能，选择没有调查员的地点），然后横置。无论该敌人是否与攻击它的调查员交战，这个效果都会发生。

本战役中的某些敌人拥有巡逻关键词。在敌军阶段（框架步骤 3.2）中，每个处于重整状态且未交战、拥有巡逻关键词的敌人，会沿着通往指定地点（写在其巡逻字样旁的括号中）的最短路径移动到一个相连地点。

• 如果有多个地点都符合指定地点的条件，由队长选择该敌人向哪个地点移动。

• 如果拥有巡逻关键词的敌人会因卡牌能力阻挡的路径而被迫移动到一个地点，则该敌人不移动。
[codex] 法典 1：蕾切尔嬷嬷

如果调查员们信了：

你走近时，蕾切尔嬷嬷站起身来。烤得油亮的肉与烤蔬菜丰盛地铺了一桌，令你直流口水。一切都那么美好。女家长对你说道：“昨晚我做了一个梦。一个幻象。在梦里，我不再是我自己。我是一个倒影。另一个蕾切尔。一个既不知痛苦也不知悔恨的蕾切尔。我成了我本该成为的模样：这个疲惫的尘世之我的变形。被改造。在天堂里被重塑。因为天堂正是造物从一开始就该有的样子。”

女家长抽出一把长长的仪式用刀。“但有些人还没有信。必须教会他们认清自己的位置。我需要你帮我让每一个人明白。”

将除蕾切尔嬷嬷以外的每张 居民 卡翻至其敌人面。

收集每张放置一旁的 居民 卡，并将它们逐一以敌人面朝上放入一个空地点。

移除当前议程上的所有毁灭标记，并将其与放置一旁的《待宰羔羊》议程互换。

如果调查员们对蕾切尔嬷嬷撒了谎：

你走近时，蕾切尔嬷嬷站起身来。盛宴周围苍蝇嗡嗡作响：桌上摆着双头生物的骇人菜肴，还有几只像是器官胀得离谱的烤鸡。女家长对人群说道：“昨晚我做了一个梦。梦里，我不再是我自己，而是一个倒影。另一个蕾切尔。一个既不知痛苦也不知悔恨的蕾切尔。我成了我本该成为的模样。在天堂里被重塑——”

你抓住时机，一记恰到好处的打击打断了她的遐想。蕾切尔嬷嬷踉跄后退，但随即以一种近乎不自然的力量站稳了身子。她的镇定被打破，抽出一把长长的仪式用刀，恶狠狠地瞪着你。

“你会为此后悔的，我的小羔羊。”

将蕾切尔嬷嬷翻至其敌人面，并对她造成 2 点伤害。

否则：

蕾切尔嬷嬷从餐桌旁的座位站起身来。盛宴周围苍蝇嗡嗡作响，女家长抽出一把长长的仪式用刀，将它埋进一名追随者的胸膛。其余的人几乎毫不在意，只顾把食物塞进饥饿的嘴里。“没有等量的牺牲，就不会有奇迹，”她说着，然后看向你，眼里满是怜悯。“而你的位置，就是见证这场盛宴。”

将蕾切尔嬷嬷翻至其敌人面。
[codex] 法典 2：莉亚·阿特伍德
“你在北岬矿井里看到了什么？”
什么也不说。

莉亚 1：莉亚坐在教堂后排的长椅上。“这座教堂是我和我姐姐一起盖的，”莉亚说着，眼神空茫——她似乎没有受到那股攫住山谷的诡异极乐的影响。

你必须决定（选择一项）：

莉亚 2：莉亚把一缕散落的头发别到耳后，手一直在抖。“我——我不知道。有个东西看起来像席米恩。但那不是他。或者也许是他的某一部——”她的神情硬了起来。“当然，你和你的勘察队只是来这里记录事实的。我不想这事被写进你们那份‘研究’里。再也别跟我说话。”

将莉亚·阿特伍德的关系等级设为 0。

莉亚 3：你没有追问这位山谷的厨娘任何细节，而是在寂静中坐到旁边的长椅上。森林里昆虫振翅的嗡鸣此刻听来阴森可怖。莉亚把脸埋进双手。一群赴宴者的歌声盖过了低声抽泣。

提高莉亚·阿特伍德的关系等级。每位调查员获得 1 点奖励经验。

取得莉亚·阿特伍德的控制权。

“这座教堂是我和我姐姐一起盖的，”莉亚温和地笑着。她盯着落日，眼神发直。“这一切都太美了。你感觉得到吗？我们就站在无限的边缘。等着跨过去。也许蕾切尔说得对……”

提高莉亚·阿特伍德的关系等级。每位调查员获得 1 点奖励经验。
[codex] 法典 3：席米恩·阿特伍德

“欢迎来到矿工秘密捣蛋会最重要的一次会议，”席米恩把你拉到学校的屋檐下。“现在烟火全都放好了，我们只要等对的时机把它们点着。蕾切尔姨妈准会气疯的！”他调皮地咧嘴一笑。“作为一个随时可以牺牲的小兵，你干得不错。继续保持，说不定我会给你升个职。”

提高席米恩·阿特伍德 2 级关系等级。每位调查员获得 2 点奖励经验。

取得席米恩·阿特伍德的控制权。

“准备遭殃吧！”席米恩从灌木丛里跳出来，手里拿着一根看起来像点了火的炸药。你反应迅速，一个扑身躲开，‘炸药’炸开成一团火花。你站起身来，席米恩正冲你咯咯坏笑。

提高席米恩·阿特伍德的关系等级。每位调查员获得 1 点奖励经验。

[codex] 法典 4：威廉·汉洛克

你拦住瑞玟，好让威廉把文件收拢起来。他捧着文件，双颊发红，接着便哭了起来。“我都做了些什么？这座岛毁了。全怪那个该死的蕾切尔。”

“还不算晚，”瑞玟站起身来，龇牙道。“你还能把属于我的东西给我。”

提高威廉·汉洛克的关系等级。每位调查员获得 2 点奖励经验。

取得威廉·汉洛克的控制权。

将瑞玟·霍桑的关系等级设为 0。

致亨利·阿米蒂奇博士办公室：

铁杉岛的勘察已经结束，而马奎兹博士没能回来。我们在那座荒凉岛屿上的所见所闻，完全无法用常理解释。一种异类的存在支配着当地的生态系统，扭曲了附近每一个生物的身心健康。我们见证了一些从未被记录过的物种，而且今后很可能再也无法记录。当地人与此存在共存了数十年，表面上——或者刻意地——对其退化性的影响毫不知情。有些人甚至崇拜它。我们自认能活下来已是万幸。

不幸的是，马奎兹博士没有这样的运气。随信附上一份详尽的报告，记录了她对这片独特生态系统的观察。报告里没有写到的，是她如何——以及何等英勇地——献出了自己的生命。那个故事，我们希望能当面讲给你听。出于对她遗志的敬意，我们请求你不要把这些记录当作纯粹的臆想而不予理会。谨上，

密斯卡托尼克勘察队

“我的孩子们，时刻到了，”蕾切尔嬷嬷狂喜地说。她举起双臂，模仿那座多面的雕像。人群静了下来，每个赴宴者都依次模仿起她的姿势。

结局 3：蕾切尔嬷嬷站在十字路口的雕像前，双臂像树枝一样朝天空张开。她周围的地上散落着追随者的尸骨。一股狂喜席卷全场，人群齐声叹息。“它来了！”女家长喊道。月亮暗了下来，一场月全食让一切都染上绯红。

雕像周围的地面裂开，塌陷成一个天坑。你的极乐化作恶心与剧痛，皮肤一块块脱落。你坠入一片水晶般的深渊，耳畔伴随着蕾切尔嬷嬷吟唱的一首虔敬圣歌，以及一阵奔涌的喜悦、愤怒与空虚——悲伤——好奇——渴望——绝望。

你停止呼吸，感觉自己被变形为上百个另外的自己：有人类也有非人，有生者也有死者，有年少也有苍老。你向上望去，望见一团翻涌的瘴气之云，只见蕾切尔嬷嬷已变形为一个被雾气环绕、光辉四射的玻璃质形体。这里就是你的位置。你的目的。你的血肉硬化成灰色的岩石，又变成玻璃般的水晶，你伸手向上，竭力去触碰她那神圣的形貌。

然后，是一片冰冷而寂静的空无。

The Feast of Hemlock Vale campaign features a new gameplay concept: The Codex. During this campaign, some card effects may direct players to read a specific codex entry. While playing, keep the Campaign Guide on hand for easy reference.

Certain locations, characters, or enemies in The Feast of Hemlock Vale have codex entries, marked with ([codex] X). To read a character or location’s codex entry, you must pay all costs on that ability first, then turn to the current scenario or prelude’s Codex in this Campaign Guide and resolve all text.

• Each codex entry cannot be resolved more than once per scenario or prelude unless otherwise stated.

• When resolving a codex entry, the player who triggered that entry resolves all effects (resolving a test, dealing damage, paying resources, etc.). If it is unclear who triggered the codex entry, the lead investigator resolves the entry.

• If a codex entry instructs players to put a named set-aside resident into play, put that character into play with their story asset side faceup unless otherwise stated.

• A resident whose name is crossed out in your Campaign Log cannot enter play during preludes or scenarios. If a resident’s name is crossed out, so are all entries in that resident’s Notes.

• While resolving a codex entry for a specific character, you may only read a single section for which you meet the requirements. If you do not meet the requirements for the first section of a codex entry, skip to the following section. Only refer to that character’s Notes and Relationship Level in your Campaign Log unless otherwise stated. (e.g. “In River Hawthorne’s Notes, record River is a dreamboat” directs players to change the “Notes” section in River’s Campaign Log entry.)

• After resolving a codex entry and making any changes in your Campaign Log, resume play.

The Feast of Hemlock Vale campaign gives players just three days in-game to play out its story. This campaign also contains playable preludes in which investigators may interact with the residents of Hemlock Vale, learn the secrets of Hemlock Isle, and make preparations for the next scenario. Preludes are non-confrontational segments that are set up with locations and a scenario reference, act, and agenda. The end of each prelude provides several choices on which scenario to play next. Depending on the day and time, some scenarios may provide new story options or challenges. Players will not have time to play every scenario or befriend each resident on a single playthrough of this campaign.

• Players may earn experience when playing preludes and interludes. Record this experience under “Unspent Experience,” but do not spend it until instructed to by the campaign guide.

• To keep track of the current day/time, you may refer to and update the “Day/Time” section in the Campaign Log.

At times, story text may instruct investigators to increase their Relationship Level with a particular resident. If instructed to do so, check the Campaign Log and find the specified resident’s entry.

• When referring to a resident’s Relationship Level, the number of checked boxes in their entry is that resident’s Relationship Level.

• To increase a resident’s Relationship Level, check the leftmost unchecked box in that resident’s entry.

• To decrease a resident’s Relationship Level, erase the rightmost checked box in that resident’s entry.

• Unless otherwise stated, you should increase or decrease a resident’s Relationship Level by 1 box at a time.

• If instructed to set a resident’s Relationship Level to 0, erase all checked boxes in that resident’s entry.

• A resident whose name is crossed out in your Campaign Log cannot enter play during preludes or scenarios.

Most scenarios in this campaign are arranged in a set grid pattern. During these scenarios, each location is connected to each location adjacent to it, in addition to any connection icons.

• Adjacent locations share a side (left, right, above, or below). Locations that share only a corner are not considered adjacent.

• When instructed to put a location into play, place it in an adjacent empty space above, below, or to the left or right of your location.

• You cannot put a location into play where an existing location already is. When choosing where to put a new location, you must choose a spot unoccupied by a location, if able. If you cannot, no new locations are put into play.

• Note that during preludes and scenarios that utilize The Vale encounter set, locations are only connected via their icons.

Some enemies in this campaign have the alert keyword. Each time an investigator fails a skill test while attempting to evade an enemy with the alert keyword, after applying all results for that skill test, that enemy performs an attack against the evading investigator. An enemy does not exhaust after performing an alert attack. This attack occurs whether the enemy is engaged with the evading investigator or not.

During setup during this campaign, players may be instructed to put the Time Marker card into play. To do so, find the Time Marker card in the The First Day, The Second Day, or The Final Day encounter sets that corresponds to the current day and place it next to the agenda deck. This is the current day and time.

Some cards have different effects depending on whether the scenario takes place during the Day or Night. Text following a (Day [day]) or (Night [night]) keyword is only active if the scenario or prelude being played is during the Day or Night, respectively. Any other ability not preceded by these keywords is active regardless of the time period.

Setup instructions may have specific instructions depending on the current day and time. (e.g. “If it is Day 2, put River Hawthorne into play at the Cranberry Bog” only applies when playing that scenario as a Day 2 scenario and not a Night 2 scenario).

Some enemies in this campaign have the elusive keyword. Elusive enemies represent enemies who want to avoid the investigators for their own survival or to accomplish their own goals.

If a ready enemy with the elusive keyword attacks or is attacked, after that attack resolves, that enemy immediately disengages from all investigators, moves to a connecting location (with no investigators, if able), and exhausts. This effect occurs whether the enemy was engaged with the attacking investigator or not.

Some enemies in this campaign have the patrol keyword. During the enemy phase (in framework step 3.2), each ready, unengaged enemy with the patrol keyword moves to a connecting location along the shortest path toward the designated location (as described in parentheses next to the word patrol).

• If there are multiple locations that qualify as the designated location, the lead investigator may choose which location the enemy moves toward.

• If an enemy with patrol would be compelled to move to a location via a path that is blocked by a card ability, the enemy does not move.

The Feast of Hemlock Vale campaign features a new gameplay concept: The Codex. During this campaign, some card effects may direct players to read a specific codex entry. While playing, keep the Campaign Guide on hand for easy reference.

Certain locations, characters, or enemies in The Feast of Hemlock Vale have codex entries, marked with ([codex] X). To read a character or location’s codex entry, you must pay all costs on that ability first, then turn to the current scenario or prelude’s Codex in this Campaign Guide and resolve all text.

• Each codex entry cannot be resolved more than once per scenario or prelude unless otherwise stated.

• When resolving a codex entry, the player who triggered that entry resolves all effects (resolving a test, dealing damage, paying resources, etc.). If it is unclear who triggered the codex entry, the lead investigator resolves the entry.

• If a codex entry instructs players to put a named set-aside resident into play, put that character into play with their story asset side faceup unless otherwise stated.

Three Days, Three Nights

The Feast of Hemlock Vale campaign gives players just three days in-game to play out its story. This campaign also contains playable preludes in which investigators may interact with the residents of Hemlock Vale, learn the secrets of Hemlock Isle, and make preparations for the next scenario.

Preludes are non-confrontational segments that are set up with locations and a scenario reference, act, and agenda. The end of each prelude provides several choices on which scenario to play next. Depending on the day and time, some scenarios may provide new story options or challenges. Players will not have time to play every scenario or befriend each resident on a single playthrough of this campaign.

• Players may earn experience when playing preludes and interludes. Record this experience under “Unspent Experience,” but do not spend it until instructed to by the campaign guide.

• To keep track of the current day/time, you may refer to and update the “Day/Time” section in the Campaign Log.

Residents & Relationship Levels

At times, story text may instruct investigators to increase their Relationship Level with a particular resident. If instructed to do so, check the Campaign Log and find the specified resident’s entry.

• When referring to a resident’s Relationship Level, the number of checked boxes in their entry is that resident’s Relationship Level.

• To increase a resident’s Relationship Level, check the leftmost unchecked box in that resident’s entry.

• To decrease a resident’s Relationship Level, erase the rightmost checked box in that resident’s entry.

• Unless otherwise stated, you should increase or decrease a resident’s Relationship Level by 1 box at a time.

• If instructed to set a resident’s Relationship Level to 0, erase all checked boxes in that resident’s entry.

• A resident whose name is crossed out in your Campaign Log cannot enter play during preludes or scenarios.

Location Adjacency in this Campaign

Most scenarios in this campaign are arranged in a set grid pattern. During these scenarios, each location is connected to each location adjacent to it, in addition to any connection icons.

• Adjacent locations share a side (left, right, above, or below). Locations that share only a corner are not considered adjacent.

• When instructed to put a location into play, place it in an adjacent empty space above, below, or to the left or right of your location.

• You cannot put a location into play where an existing location already is. When choosing where to put a new location, you must choose a spot unoccupied by a location, if able. If you cannot, no new locations are put into play.

• Note that during preludes and scenarios that utilize The Vale encounter set, locations are only connected via their icons.

Alert

Some enemies in this campaign have the alert keyword. Each time an investigator fails a skill test while attempting to evade an enemy with the alert keyword, after applying all results for that skill test, that enemy performs an attack against the evading investigator. An enemy does not exhaust after performing an alert attack. This attack occurs whether the enemy is engaged with the evading investigator or not.

Day [day] and Night [night]

During setup during this campaign, players may be instructed to put the Time Marker card into play. To do so, find the Time Marker card in the The First Day, The Second Day, or The Final Day encounter sets that corresponds to the current day and place it next to the agenda deck. This is the current day and time.

Some cards have different effects depending on whether the scenario takes place during the Day or Night. Text following a (Day [day]) or (Night [night]) keyword is only active if the scenario or prelude being played is during the Day or Night, respectively. Any other ability not preceded by these keywords is active regardless of the time period.

Setup instructions may have specific instructions depending on the current day and time. (e.g. “If it is Day 2, put River Hawthorne into play at the Cranberry Bog” only applies when playing that scenario as a Day 2 scenario and not a Night 2 scenario).

Elusive

Some enemies in this campaign have the elusive keyword. Elusive enemies represent enemies who want to avoid the investigators for their own survival or to accomplish their own goals.

If a ready enemy with the elusive keyword attacks or is attacked, after that attack resolves, that enemy immediately disengages from all investigators, moves to a connecting location (with no investigators, if able), and exhausts. This effect occurs whether the enemy was engaged with the attacking investigator or not.

Patrol

Some enemies in this campaign have the patrol keyword. During the enemy phase (in framework step 3.2), each ready, unengaged enemy with the patrol keyword moves to a connecting location along the shortest path toward the designated location (as described in parentheses next to the word patrol).

• If there are multiple locations that qualify as the designated location, the lead investigator may choose which location the enemy moves toward.

• If an enemy with patrol would be compelled to move to a location via a path that is blocked by a card ability, the enemy does not move.

Resolution 1: The evening chatter fades as residents trickle out of the Commons. There is an uncharacteristic spring in Dr. Marquez’s step as you reconvene outside the Commons. The sunset casts the sky in shades from ochre, to lilac, to violet. The professor cracks a handful of walnuts as you share your impressions of Hemlock Isle.

“This island has the density and special variance of a jungle, but it’s far more dangerous than any jungle. I have no clue why someone would start a commune in such a hazardous environment, but I understand it wasn’t always so deadly. Something was introduced and fundamentally changed the local ecosystem,” Dr. Marquez muses.

You mention the unusually good mood shared by everyone in the village, and the professor nods. “Most everyone looks blissed out of their minds. It’s like walking into an opium den. But as far as I can tell, the food isn’t laced with anything. Though I didn’t try the bread pudding. I’ve never liked bread, and the last time I had pudding was in Oxford.”

The professor’s reference to the prestigious university brings Bertie Musgrave to mind, and you ask where he is.

“You haven’t seen him? I assumed he went back to the boarding house to rest,” she scowls. “Theo offered to lend us his truck for the evening. I thought we could observe some of the local wildlife at night, but I suppose we should find him first.”

A heavy breeze stirs the trees and grass around you, smelling of cedar and pine. Dr. Marquez grips her cane. “If you’d rather take the truck and continue the survey, I can look for Bertie on my own.”

Resolution 3: You share your own observations of Hemlock Isle. More than just ‘wonders,’ the creatures here are either sickly and malnourished, or aggressively vivacious. Dr. Marquez nods along. “Everything is affected. Sickly. Starving. Mutating. And it’s all highly localized. There are no reports of these strange phenomena elsewhere. It’s only here.” She produces a creased map of the island and points to the north hills. “Pearl Ridge hasn’t recovered in the past twenty years since it was obliterated.”

Marquez holds up two rings of glassy wood from both Eastwick Bog and Pearl Orchard, then draws a ring around Pearl Ridge on her map. “The bitter eggs this morning reminded me of a report after the Tunguska event. A meteorite obliterated miles of Russian countryside, but the effects on the locals were even more devastating. Stores of food were poisoned. Livestock perished. Nearby villages were slowly deserted as families who lived there for generations died of starvation or worse.” She draws a larger concentric circle around the first.

“Nobody has said anything about a meteor, but judging by the massive sinkhole in front of the Pearl Estate, something emerged from the rock. My working theory is that the mining operation opened a vein and released whatever poisoned gas or mineral affecting the island.”

Dr. Marquez’s expression goes grave. “There’s something else. Something we shouldn’t discuss here. Follow me.” As you follow the professor out of the Commons, a stout figure bumps into you.

I would love to—” Dr. Marquez cuts him off with a sharp glance. “After last night, Bertie, I think it’s best if you stay in your room tonight and rest.” The young assistant looks quite wounded, but doesn’t object. “Very well then,” he mutters.

The people in the—” he gestures to the crowd around. “The place. I had an epiphany but I quite forgot it. Mother Rachel has been taking care of me. They told me there will be more dancing later, in the crossroads, and a large bonfire.”

“You need to rest. Head back to the boarding house,” Marquez insists. You can’t be sure if Bertie even heard her as he slips away.

Something big and hungry. I tried to take shelter at the old Atwood Farm, but it was boarded up. Windows and doors. It smelled something awful. I’m not even sure what I heard coming from inside,” she says soberly. When you ask her to explain, she shakes her head.

“This place definitely isn’t what it seems. I don’t know what the Vale folks are hiding in that old farmhouse, but I plan to find out.”

Judith’s hunting jacket is splattered with blood and her hair is a mess as she approaches you, rifle slung over her shoulder. I was gonna ask where you’re headed next.”

You tell her you’re headed to Arkham, and she suppresses a snort of disbelief. “Arkham, huh? The city that’s in the news with weird shit every other week? You’re really headed back there?” She goes quiet for a moment as if considering something. “You’re going to need someone to watch your back,” she ventures. You tell her you plan to take a long rest, and she smirks. “I’ve got a buddy who runs a speakeasy somewhere in Easttown. After everything we’ve been through, I’d say I owe you a drink.”

[codex] Codex 8: Theo Peters

Theo grins sheepishly as you approach, then wraps you in a bear hug. As he pulls away, you see he is crying. After mom and pop passed, Helen got—she got tough. And then I started to help out around the Vale, and they didn’t care how tough I was. It felt like home. And now that’s gone too.” He blinks tears from his eyes. “I guess home is what you make it. You should come visit us in Portland some time. I know you’ll love it,” he smiles.

Epilogue 1: June 1926

To the office of Dr. Henry Armitage,

The survey of Hemlock Isle has concluded without Dr. Marquez. What we found there on that desolate island defies reason. An alien presence dominated the local ecosystem, warping the physical and mental wellbeing of every living thing in its proximity. We witnessed species that have never been documented before, and likely never will be again. The locals coexisted with this presence for decades, seemingly or intentionally unaware of its degenerative effects. Some even worshiped it. We count ourselves lucky to have survived.

Dr. Marquez, unfortunately, was not so lucky. Enclosed with this letter is a comprehensive account detailing her observations of this unique ecosystem. What it does not contain is the story of how—and how bravely—she gave her life. That is a story we wish to share with you in person. We ask, out of respect for her memory, that you not dismiss these records as mere fantasy. Faithfully yours,

The Miskatonic Survey

Epilogue 2: June 1926

To the office of Dr. Henry Armitage,

The survey of Hemlock Isle has concluded at great cost. Over the course of our three day excursion, we witnessed horrors and wonders that defy all reason. A parasitic life form unlike any other fed on the local ecosystem, warping the biology of every living thing around it. I have enclosed a comprehensive account of the phenomena we witnessed, along with samples, notes, and sketches.

Although I was initially wary of your contacts, they provided invaluable support throughout the survey. Ultimately, the strange gaseous entity we discovered took their lives. Without their sacrifice, I would have perished, along with most of Hemlock Isle.

I will explain everything in further detail upon my return.

Dr. Rosa Marquez

Epilogue 3: June 1926

To the office of Dr. Henry Armitage,

The survey of Hemlock Isle has concluded. Over the course of our three day excursion, we witnessed horrors and wonders that defy all reason. I will explain everything in further detail upon my return. Until then, the survey team and I plan to take a long-deserved rest.

Dr. Rosa Marquez

Resolution 1: Mother Rachel staggers back, clutching her side. “Don’t you see our true purpose? We are light coiled in flesh. And the flesh longs to join an even greater light: an infinite and eternal brilliance.” The matron casts off her cloak, flecked with blood, to bare her shoulder. Her skin is knotted like bark with glowing nodes and alien patterns. Suddenly, the moon darkens in a total lunar eclipse, casting everything in crimson.

“My children, the hour is at hand,” Mother Rachel says rapturously. She raises her arms up to mimic the many-faced effigy. A hush falls over the crowd as each of the revelers mimics her pose in turn.

• Skip to Resolution 4.

Resolution 2: You stammer an apology, but Mother Rachel holds one hand up to silence you and says dispassionately, “You failed me. But I suppose I was wrong to ask so much of you. All things move toward their end. You were called to witness the final miracle. The heavenly ascendance. And witness it you shall.”

• Proceed to Resolution 3.

Resolution 3: Mother Rachel stands before the effigy in the crossroads, her arms unfurled like branches toward the sky. The ground around her is littered with the bones and the corpses of her followers. The crowd sighs in unison as a rush of euphoria spreads through the room. “It is here!” the matron shouts. The moon darkens in a total lunar eclipse, casting everything in crimson.

The earth around the effigy cracks as it collapses into a sinkhole. Your bliss gives way to nausea and acute pain as your skin sloughs off in patches. As you freefall into a crystalline abyss, you are accompanied by Mother Rachel’s voice singing a reverent hymn, accompanied by a rush of joy, of anger and emptiness—sorrow—curiosity—longing—despair.

Your breath stops as you feel yourself transfigured into a hundred other versions of yourself: human and inhuman, alive and dead, young and old. As you stare upward at a roiling, miasmic cloud, you see Mother Rachel tranfigured into an effulgent, glassy shape wreathed in mist. This is your place. Your purpose. As your flesh hardens into gray rock, then glassy crystal, you reach up, straining to touch her divine shape.

And then, a cold and quiet emptiness.

• Or at least, this version of each investigator is devoured. As you ascend, you see other versions of yourself. You may replay this prelude to try for a different outcome.

Resolution 4: “That’s enough,” Dr. Marquez strides past the grinning revelers and strikes Mother Rachel with her cane. She turns to exhort the crowd. “It’s not too late! We can still leave!” You shout your support. Mother Rachel lurches to her feet, drunkenly holding the ceremonial knife, and swings weakly at the professor. Marquez pushes her away with a well-timed kick.

The earth around the effigy cracks with prismatic light, then turns blindingly bright as the pillar collapses into crystalline shards. A blinding pillar of light shoots out of the nearby well. All you hear as the crossroads collapse is Mother Rachel’s empty laughter.
